name: W1
notes: From the creator's own hands-on comparison video (Tanchjim Hexa*, EQ'd dongle setup — *IEM name per auto-transcript, unconfirmed): thin, non-tacky silicone that still grips surprisingly well — called it 'one of the best' fits he's tried, comfortable even worn loose, works for both shallow and deep insertion. Doesn't attract dust since it isn't tacky. Barely touches the existing tuning/EQ but noticeably widens the soundstage — his 'sweet spot.' Cheapest of the six tips in the comparison and still his explicit S pick and new daily driver.

name: Sedna Earfit Mythril
notes: Reputation-based placement, not a hands-on test — this one wasn't part of the creator's 6-tip comparison (Dunu S&S, Crystal 2, Magic Form Tips, CoreIR Brass, EarrBond EBT, SpinFit W1), so treat it as the least confident entry on the list. The metal-reinforced-nozzle variant of Azla's Sedna Earfit line; the rigid core is generally reported to tighten bass and sharpen treble extension versus the stock silicone version, at the cost of a slightly firmer, less plush feel in the ear than Crystal 2.

name: Sedna Earfit Crystal 2
notes: From the creator's hands-on comparison: thicker silicone core than standard tips, feels premium in hand, zero itching even on his sensitive skin ('is this medical grade silicone?'). Deep-fit gives solid, tight bass and vocals but narrows the soundstage; shallow-fit opens the stage back up at some cost to clarity (possibly the wax guard mesh, possibly placebo per his own caveat). Comfortable enough that he placed it just above Dunu S&S — a modest 'A-.'

name: S&S Eartips
notes: From the creator's hands-on comparison: cheap-feeling, thin, bouncy silicone that was a tight, awkward push onto the nozzle. Sits shallow on the ear rather than inserting deep, gripping via a tacky surface. Gave a fairly big bass bump and wider soundstage, but lost background detail and clarity — sounded 'moody'/darker, though still enjoyable. The tacky material caused itching on his sensitive skin after extended wear and picks up dust when not in use. His own verdict: 'Solid B.'

name: EBT
notes: From the creator's hands-on comparison: silicone-over-memory-foam hybrid with a stainless-steel nozzle insert. Comfortable, soft-smooth material and excellent noise isolation from the foam core, but doesn't grip the ear enough for a shallow fit — has to go in deep. The metal insert is his suspected cause of a strong, painful sibilance on female vocals, sharp enough that he cross-checked against Crystal 2 to confirm it wasn't the source. Physically comfortable to wear but uncomfortable to actually listen through — landed as a reluctant 'low B' after waffling toward C.

name: CoreIR Brass
notes: From the creator's hands-on comparison: the priciest tip he owns, with a visible brass reinforcement core. Slick silicone like SpinFit but not omnidirectional — needs an exact, firm-pressed fit to feel right at all. Thinned out mid-bass, pushed vocals too far forward, and made the sound 'showy'/tinny with strong, painful sibilance on female vocals. Narrowed the soundstage and made his IEM too bright for his taste. His own comparison: he'd rather wear the itchy Dunu S&S for 3 hours than this.

name: Magic Form Tips
notes: From the creator's hands-on comparison: memory-foam tip with an internal rubber/elastic core, firmer than a standard foam tip and with a rougher exterior texture. Bass got softer/fuller and sibilance was smoothed away by the foam, but the foam doesn't conform to his ear the way normal memory foam does — it presses back toward its molded shape instead, creating real pressure in the canal and, per his notes, made the inside of his ear hot. He says comfort is the single most important factor in an eartip, and on that axis this was his worst — an explicit D, with the plain stock foam tips from his own IEM preferred over it at similar sound quality.
